### *class* ek.qe.decide.ConformalGate(alpha=0.1, nonconformity=<function ConformalGate.<lambda>>, q=inf, \_cal=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Split-conformal accept/flag with a finite-sample **marginal** guarantee.

Fit on `(calibrated_prob, correct)`: the nonconformity scores of the *correct*
calibration items set a threshold `q` such that, among truly-correct test items
exchangeable with them, at most `alpha` are flagged. The guarantee is
*marginal*, not per-field-type – use [`GroupConformalGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.GroupConformalGate) for that.

* **Parameters:**
  * **alpha** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Target false-flag rate on correct items (e.g. `0.1`).
  * **nonconformity** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Maps calibrated confidence -> nonconformity (default
    `1 - confidence`: low confidence is nonconforming).

#### fit(probs, correct)

Fit `q` from the nonconformity scores of the *correct* calibration items.

Non-finite confidences are dropped (a single `NaN` would otherwise sort to
the end and corrupt the quantile, silently breaking the coverage guarantee).

* **Return type:**
  [`ConformalGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.ConformalGate)

#### p_value(confidence)

Per-instance conformal p-value (small = atypical of correct items).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### *class* ek.qe.decide.CostSensitiveGate(rho=1.0, block_threshold=0.0, accept_threshold=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Accept/flag/block from the cost ratio `rho = c_FN / c_FP` on calibrated `p`.

Accept when the expected cost of accepting is below that of routing to a human.
Accepting risks an undetected error: cost `(1 - p) * c_FN`. Flagging a value
that was actually *correct* wastes a review: cost `p * c_FP` (the false-positive
cost is incurred only with probability `p`, not unconditionally). So accept iff
`(1 - p) * c_FN <= p * c_FP`, i.e. the Bayes-optimal threshold
`p >= c_FN / (c_FN + c_FP) = rho / (1 + rho)`. A larger `rho` (misses much
costlier than reviews) raises the bar to auto-accept (`tau -> 1` as
`rho -> inf`); `rho = 1` gives the symmetric `tau = 0.5`.
`block_threshold` adds an optional hard-fail band at the bottom.

* **Parameters:**
  * **rho** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Cost ratio `c_FN / c_FP` (>= 0). The single lever; no magic numbers.
  * **block_threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Calibrated probability at or below which to `block` rather
    than `flag` (default `0` -> never block on probability alone; a
    failed verifier is what forces a block, upstream).
  * **accept_threshold** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Override the derived accept threshold explicitly.

#### *property* tau *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

The accept threshold on calibrated probability (derived from `rho`).

### ek.qe.decide.DEFAULT_ALPHA *= 0.1*

Default target miscoverage for conformal gates (flag at most ~alpha of correct items).

### ek.qe.decide.DEFAULT_RISK_TARGET *= 0.05*

Default risk bound for [`RiskControlGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.RiskControlGate) (accepted-error rate ceiling).

### *class* ek.qe.decide.GroupConformalGate(alpha=0.1, nonconformity=<function GroupConformalGate.<lambda>>, by_group=dict(), pooled=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Mondrian (class-conditional) conformal: one [`ConformalGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.ConformalGate) per group.

Restores approximate per-field-type validity by calibrating separately per group
key (e.g. `NodeType`/`FieldSpec`), with a pooled fallback for unseen groups.

### *class* ek.qe.decide.RiskControlGate(target=0.05, loss=<function RiskControlGate.<lambda>>, loss_bound=1.0, lam=1.0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Conformal Risk Control: accept `p >= lambda` bounding the accepted-error rate.

Picks the *smallest* threshold `lambda` (the most coverage) whose finite-sample
risk bound is at or below `target`. The controlled quantity is
`E[ loss(item) * 1(accepted) ]` – with the default 0/1 loss, the population
rate of accepted-yet-wrong items.

* **Parameters:**
  * **target** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Upper bound on the accepted-error rate (e.g. `0.05`).
  * **loss** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – `correct -> loss` in `[0, loss_bound]`; default `0` if correct
    else `1`. Any monotone loss bounded by `loss_bound` works.
  * **loss_bound** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – The loss’s upper bound `B` – the CRC finite-sample slack is
    `+B/(n+1)`. Must match `loss`’s range or the guarantee is invalid;
    keep the default `1.0` for the 0/1 loss.

#### fit(probs, correct)

Find the smallest accept threshold whose risk bound is <= `target`.

* **Return type:**
  [`RiskControlGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.RiskControlGate)

### ek.qe.decide.crepes_mondrian_gate(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

A Mondrian (class-conditional) conformal gate backed by `crepes` (`ek[calibration]`).

The pure-Python [`GroupConformalGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.GroupConformalGate) is the dependency-free default; use
this for parity with a crepes/sklearn conformal stack (full CDFs, normalised
variants). Raises an actionable install hint if `crepes` is absent.

### ek.qe.decide.risk_coverage_curve(probs, correct, , thresholds=None)

The risk-coverage trade-off: `{threshold, coverage, selective_risk}` per point.

Coverage is the fraction auto-accepted at each threshold; selective risk is the
error rate *among the accepted*. Lower-left is better; pick the operating point
against a target risk or coverage.

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### ek.qe.decide.split_conformal_quantile(scores, alpha)

The split-conformal threshold: the `ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) / n` empirical quantile.

`scores` are nonconformity scores on an exchangeable calibration set. Returns
`+inf` when `n` is too small to guarantee `1 - alpha` (so nothing is
flagged – the honest behaviour at that sample size), and `-inf` at the
`alpha -> 1` limit (flag everything).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)


# _autosummary/ek.qe.html.md

# ek.qe

Reference-free quality estimation: the `estimate_quality()` side of `ek`.

This package implements the online (no-gold) half of evaluation as the strict
pipeline `signal -> calibrate -> validate -> decide` (`misc/docs/ek_03`):

- **signals** (cheapest first): the deterministic [`VerifierSignal`](_autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md#ek.qe.verifiers.VerifierSignal)
  (schema/checksum/cross-field, cost tier 1, runs always), free intrinsic
  [`IntrinsicConfidenceSignal`](_autosummary/ek.qe.signals.html.md#ek.qe.signals.IntrinsicConfidenceSignal) / [`LogprobSignal`](_autosummary/ek.qe.signals.html.md#ek.qe.signals.LogprobSignal)
  > (tier 2), and the flagship ROVER [`AgreementSignal`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.AgreementSignal) multi-engine
  > vote (tier 3);
- **calibrate** – [`PlattCalibrator`](_autosummary/ek.qe.calibrate.html.md#ek.qe.calibrate.PlattCalibrator) (default) / isotonic /
  temperature, with Mondrian grouping and ECE diagnostics: \*non-optional before any
  gate\*;
- **decide** – [`CostSensitiveGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.CostSensitiveGate) (default),
  [`ConformalGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.ConformalGate), and [`RiskControlGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.RiskControlGate),
  > reading only calibrated probabilities.

Everything is pure-Python and dependency-free by default; the `ek[calibration]`
(netcal/sklearn/MAPIE/crepes) and `ek[agreement]` (uqlm) extras supply
library-backed equivalents, imported lazily so `import ek` stays light.

Importing this package registers the built-in strategies (signals, aggregators,
checks, calibrators, policies) by name in [`ek.registry`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#module-ek.registry).

### *class* ek.qe.AgreementSignal(cost_tier=3, use_confidence=True, conf_weight=0.5, null_conf=0.7, tokenize=None, max_tokens=5000)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

ROVER multi-engine agreement as a reference-free [`Signal`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Signal).

Cost tier 3 (`N` engine runs): try the deterministic verifier layer and any
free intrinsic confidence first. Called on a collection of hypotheses, it runs
[`rover()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.rover) and returns the mean per-position agreement as the raw signal –
*uncalibrated*, like every signal, so it must pass through a
[`Calibrator`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Calibrator) before any gate reads it.

### Example

```pycon
>>> sig = AgreementSignal()
>>> round(sig(["the cat sat", "the cat sit", "the bat sat"]), 3)
0.778
```

### *class* ek.qe.ConformalGate(alpha=0.1, nonconformity=<function ConformalGate.<lambda>>, q=inf, \_cal=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Split-conformal accept/flag with a finite-sample **marginal** guarantee.

Fit on `(calibrated_prob, correct)`: the nonconformity scores of the *correct*
calibration items set a threshold `q` such that, among truly-correct test items
exchangeable with them, at most `alpha` are flagged. The guarantee is
*marginal*, not per-field-type – use [`GroupConformalGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.GroupConformalGate) for that.

* **Parameters:**
  * **alpha** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Target false-flag rate on correct items (e.g. `0.1`).
  * **nonconformity** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Maps calibrated confidence -> nonconformity (default
    `1 - confidence`: low confidence is nonconforming).

#### fit(probs, correct)

Fit `q` from the nonconformity scores of the *correct* calibration items.

Non-finite confidences are dropped (a single `NaN` would otherwise sort to
the end and corrupt the quantile, silently breaking the coverage guarantee).

* **Return type:**
  [`ConformalGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.ConformalGate)

#### p_value(confidence)

Per-instance conformal p-value (small = atypical of correct items).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### *class* ek.qe.CostSensitiveGate(rho=1.0, block_threshold=0.0, accept_threshold=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Accept/flag/block from the cost ratio `rho = c_FN / c_FP` on calibrated `p`.

Accept when the expected cost of accepting is below that of routing to a human.
Accepting risks an undetected error: cost `(1 - p) * c_FN`. Flagging a value
that was actually *correct* wastes a review: cost `p * c_FP` (the false-positive
cost is incurred only with probability `p`, not unconditionally). So accept iff
`(1 - p) * c_FN <= p * c_FP`, i.e. the Bayes-optimal threshold
`p >= c_FN / (c_FN + c_FP) = rho / (1 + rho)`. A larger `rho` (misses much
costlier than reviews) raises the bar to auto-accept (`tau -> 1` as
`rho -> inf`); `rho = 1` gives the symmetric `tau = 0.5`.
`block_threshold` adds an optional hard-fail band at the bottom.

* **Parameters:**
  * **rho** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Cost ratio `c_FN / c_FP` (>= 0). The single lever; no magic numbers.
  * **block_threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Calibrated probability at or below which to `block` rather
    than `flag` (default `0` -> never block on probability alone; a
    failed verifier is what forces a block, upstream).
  * **accept_threshold** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Override the derived accept threshold explicitly.

#### *property* tau *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

The accept threshold on calibrated probability (derived from `rho`).

### *class* ek.qe.GroupCalibrator(factory=<class 'ek.qe.calibrate.PlattCalibrator'>, by_group=dict(), pooled=None, kind='group')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Per-group (Mondrian) calibration: one calibrator per `NodeType`/`FieldSpec`.

Distribution-free *conditional* (per-field-type) coverage is impossible
in general (Barber et al. 2019); calibrating separately per group restores it
approximately. `fit` takes a parallel `groups` sequence; `__call__` routes
by group key, falling back to a pooled calibrator for unseen groups.

* **Parameters:**
  **factory** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – Zero-arg callable producing a fresh per-group calibrator (default
  [`PlattCalibrator`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.PlattCalibrator)).

#### factory

alias of [`PlattCalibrator`](_autosummary/ek.qe.calibrate.html.md#ek.qe.calibrate.PlattCalibrator)

#### fit(scores, correct, , groups)

Fit one calibrator per distinct group key, plus a pooled fallback.

* **Return type:**
  [`GroupCalibrator`](_autosummary/ek.qe.calibrate.html.md#ek.qe.calibrate.GroupCalibrator)

#### to_dict()

Serialize each per-group calibrator (keyed by stringified group) plus the
pooled fallback, so a fitted Mondrian calibrator round-trips like the others.
Group keys are stringified (they are `NodeType`/`FieldSpec` names).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### *class* ek.qe.IntrinsicConfidenceSignal(pool='min', cost_tier=2)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Aggregate an extractor’s per-unit confidences into a field score.

### *class* ek.qe.IsotonicCalibrator(x=list(), y=list(), kind='isotonic')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Isotonic (monotonic non-decreasing) calibration via pool-adjacent-violators.

  * **cost_tier** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – `2` – free intrinsic signal (already computed at inference).

### *class* ek.qe.PlattCalibrator(a=1.0, b=0.0, max_iter=100, kind='platt')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Platt scaling: `sigmoid(a * score + b)`, fit by Newton/IRLS on labels.

The default calibrator: works on any scalar (aggregated confidence/logprob), no
logits required. Uses Platt’s target smoothing so it does not overfit small
calibration sets.

* **Parameters:**
  **max_iter** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Newton iterations (converges in a handful for a 2-parameter model).

#### fit(scores, correct)

Fit `a, b` to maximise the likelihood of `correct` given `scores`.

* **Return type:**
  [`PlattCalibrator`](_autosummary/ek.qe.calibrate.html.md#ek.qe.calibrate.PlattCalibrator)

### *class* ek.qe.RiskControlGate(target=0.05, loss=<function RiskControlGate.<lambda>>, loss_bound=1.0, lam=1.0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Conformal Risk Control: accept `p >= lambda` bounding the accepted-error rate.

Picks the *smallest* threshold `lambda` (the most coverage) whose finite-sample
risk bound is at or below `target`. The controlled quantity is
`E[ loss(item) * 1(accepted) ]` – with the default 0/1 loss, the population
rate of accepted-yet-wrong items.

* **Parameters:**
  * **target** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Upper bound on the accepted-error rate (e.g. `0.05`).
  * **loss** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – `correct -> loss` in `[0, loss_bound]`; default `0` if correct
    else `1`. Any monotone loss bounded by `loss_bound` works.
  * **loss_bound** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – The loss’s upper bound `B` – the CRC finite-sample slack is
    `+B/(n+1)`. Must match `loss`’s range or the guarantee is invalid;
    keep the default `1.0` for the 0/1 loss.

#### fit(probs, correct)

Find the smallest accept threshold whose risk bound is <= `target`.

* **Return type:**
  [`RiskControlGate`](_autosummary/ek.qe.decide.html.md#ek.qe.decide.RiskControlGate)

### *class* ek.qe.RoverConsensus(tokens=list(), slots=list(), agreement=list(), n_engines=0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The result of a ROVER pass over N hypotheses.

#### *property* mean_agreement *: [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)*

Mean per-position agreement over consensus tokens, a reference-free
confidence in `[0, 1]`: `1.0` means every engine agreed at every emitted
position; lower means at least one engine dissented.

An **empty** consensus (no token survived voting – NULL won every slot) means
the engines agreed on *nothing*, so this returns `0.0` when 2+ engines were
fused, NOT a misleading `1.0` (which would feed a maximal raw confidence to
the calibrator/gate). A single engine – or none – is vacuously `1.0`.

#### *property* text *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

The consensus transcription (space-joined winning tokens).

### *class* ek.qe.RoverSlot(entries=list(), winner=None, score=0.0, vote_share=0.0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One branch point of the transition network: each engine’s token (or NULL).

### *class* ek.qe.SignalFamilyCalibrator(calibrators=dict(), combine=<function mean_probability>, factory=<class 'ek.qe.calibrate.PlattCalibrator'>, fusion=None, kind='signal_family')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One calibrator per signal family, fused by a documented combination rule.

Averaging heterogeneous raw signals (an LLM-judge score, a token logprob, a ROVER
agreement) and calibrating the mean discards exactly what a calibrator needs:
each family has its own scale, reliability and direction of miscalibration. This
calibrates every signal *by name* with its own calibrator, then fuses the
calibrated probabilities with `combine`.

Pass it (or simply a `Mapping[str, Calibrator]`) as
`estimate_quality(..., calibrator=...)`.

**The fused value must itself be calibrated before it is gated.** Fusing
calibrated probabilities (by mean, min, …) does not yield a calibrated
probability: agreeing families make the mean under-confident, a weak family
drags it toward the base rate. So [`fit()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.SignalFamilyCalibrator.fit) also learns a second-stage
`fusion` calibrator on `combine`’s output, and `__call__` applies it.
Without a `fusion` calibrator (e.g. a hand-built mapping),
[`ek.estimate_quality()`](_autosummary/ek.html.md#ek.estimate_quality) refuses to gate a value fused from two or more
families unless told `assume_calibrated=True` (Hard Rule 1). A value from a
single family is that family’s calibrated probability and gates as is.

A field’s own upstream `confidence` is just one more family here, named
`"confidence"`: include it in the training rows under that name.

* **Parameters:**
  * **calibrators** ([`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)) – `signal name -> Calibrator`. A `"*"` entry is the fallback
    for any signal without its own entry. A signal with neither is refused
    (`ValueError`) rather than silently dropped or passed through raw
    (Hard Rule 1).
  * **combine** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – `Mapping[str, float] -> float` fusing the calibrated values;
    [`mean_probability()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.mean_probability) (default) or [`min_probability()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.min_probability), or any
    callable of that shape (e.g. a learned stacker).
  * **factory** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – Zero-arg callable producing a fresh calibrator, used by [`fit()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.SignalFamilyCalibrator.fit).
  * **fusion** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – Second-stage calibrator applied to `combine`’s output (learned by
    [`fit()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.SignalFamilyCalibrator.fit)); `None` leaves the fused value uncalibrated.

### Example

```pycon
>>> rows = [{"judge": j, "logprob": l} for j, l in
...         [(0.9, -0.1), (0.8, -0.2), (0.85, -2.0), (0.3, -0.1), (0.2, -2.5), (0.7, -1.8)]]
>>> correct = [True, True, False, True, False, False]
>>> cal = SignalFamilyCalibrator().fit(rows, correct)
>>> sorted(cal.calibrators)
['judge', 'logprob']
>>> 0.0 <= cal({"judge": 0.9, "logprob": -0.1}) <= 1.0
True
```

#### calibrate_signals(raw_signals, , group=None)

`{name: calibrated probability}` for each raw signal (before fusion).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### combine()

Fuse calibrated per-family probabilities by their mean (the default combiner).

Each family’s calibrated value estimates the *same* event (“this field is
correct”), so the mean is a defensible, assumption-light pooling rule.

```pycon
>>> mean_probability({"judge": 0.9, "logprob": 0.7})
0.8
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### factory

alias of [`PlattCalibrator`](_autosummary/ek.qe.calibrate.html.md#ek.qe.calibrate.PlattCalibrator)

#### fit(signals, correct)

Fit one calibrator per signal name, then the `fusion` calibrator.

Each family is fit over the rows where it appears with a finite value. A
family with fewer than two such rows, or only one label class, cannot be
calibrated and is refused (`ValueError`) rather than turned into a
constant that would then dilute the fusion.

* **Return type:**
  [`SignalFamilyCalibrator`](_autosummary/ek.qe.calibrate.html.md#ek.qe.calibrate.SignalFamilyCalibrator)

#### fuse(calibrated)

Fuse per-family calibrated probabilities: `combine`, then `fusion`.

A single family’s value is returned as is: it is already calibrated, and
`fusion` was learned on fused values.

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### to_dict()

Serialize every family’s calibrator and the (registered) combiner’s name.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### *class* ek.qe.TemperatureCalibrator(T=1.0, kind='temperature', t_min=0.05, t_max=10.0, max_iter=60)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Temperature scaling: `sigmoid(logit / T)` with one `T` fit on a holdout.

Use **only when you have logits**: `__call__` expects a *logit*, not a
probability. `T > 1` softens overconfidence; the argmax is unchanged.

#### fit(logits, correct)

Fit `T` by minimising NLL with a bounded 1-D search.

* **Return type:**

Golden-section search bounds and iteration count (config, not magic numbers).

### *class* ek.qe.VerifierSignal(validators=list(), cost_tier=1)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Deterministic verifier evidence as a reference-free [`Signal`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Signal).

Cost tier 1 – the free, first-to-run layer. Runs a list of
[`Validator`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Validator) s on a value and returns the **fraction that passed**
in `[0, 1]` as the raw signal (`1.0` = every check passed). It also exposes
the [`Finding`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Finding) s it produced via [`findings()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.VerifierSignal.findings), so the same
object feeds both the score path (-> calibrate) and the audit path (-> review).
Like every signal it is uncalibrated: a verifier failing is strong evidence, not
a probability, so a [`Calibrator`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Calibrator) still runs before any gate.

### Example

```pycon
>>> v = VerifierSignal([checksum_validator("luhn")])
>>> v("79927398713")          # valid -> all checks pass
1.0
>>> v("79927398710")          # invalid -> the one check fails
0.0
```

#### findings(value, , spec=None)

All findings the validators produce for `value` (empty == all clear).

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Finding)]

### ek.qe.rover(hypotheses, , use_confidence=True, conf_weight=0.5, null_conf=0.7, tokenize=None, max_tokens=5000)

Align N hypotheses, vote per slot, and emit consensus + per-position agreement.

* **Parameters:**
  * **hypotheses** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – The recognizer/extractor outputs to fuse. Each may be a string,
    an `OcrResult`-shaped object (`.text`/`.mean_confidence`), a list of
    token strings, or a list of `(token, confidence)` pairs.
  * **use_confidence** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Blend confidence into the vote (`True`) or vote purely by
    frequency (`False`, which forces `conf_weight` to `0`).
  * **conf_weight** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Weight on average confidence vs vote frequency in the slot score
    (Fiscus’s `1 - alpha`); `0` is frequency-only, `1` is
    confidence-only. Ignored when `use_confidence` is `False`.
  * **null_conf** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Confidence credited to a NULL vote (an engine that produced no
    token at a slot) – the lever for how readily a deletion wins.
  * **tokenize** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]]]) – Optional `hypothesis -> [(token, confidence), ...]` override; by
    default `_as_units()` handles strings/OcrResults/token lists.
  * **max_tokens** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Reject any hypothesis longer than this (the aligner is
    `O(N*l*L*L')`; an unbounded input is a quadratic time/memory DoS).
    `None` disables the guard.
* **Return type:**
  [`RoverConsensus`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.RoverConsensus)
* **Returns:**
  A [`RoverConsensus`](_autosummary/ek.qe.html.md#ek.qe.RoverConsensus) with the consensus `tokens`/`text`, the per-slot
  breakdown, and the per-consensus-token `agreement` usable as a raw signal.

### ek.qe.split_conformal_quantile(scores, alpha)

The split-conformal threshold: the `ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) / n` empirical quantile.

`scores` are nonconformity scores on an exchangeable calibration set. Returns
`+inf` when `n` is too small to guarantee `1 - alpha` (so nothing is
flagged – the honest behaviour at that sample size), and `-inf` at the
`alpha -> 1` limit (flag everything).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

Flag when `record[total_key]` does not equal the sum of `item_keys` (±tol).

The canonical cross-field check (invoice total = Σ line items). Skipped (rather
than raising or flagging) when the total or *all* item keys are absent or
non-numeric, so it is safe on partial records.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Finding)]

# _autosummary/ek.qe.signals.html.md

# ek.qe.signals

Intrinsic confidence signals: token logprobs and per-unit posteriors (cost tier 2).

When the extractor already emits something usable – token log-probabilities
(generative locals like TrOCR/pix2tex, GPT-4o, Mistral OCR) or per-unit posteriors
(Google Cloud Vision, Azure, Tesseract) – the cheapest reliable signal is *free*:
it was computed during inference. This module turns those raw numbers into a single
field-level score (`misc/docs/ek_03` §1a). Two modelling facts drive the design:

1. **Raw summed logprob is length-biased** – longer fields accumulate more negative
   terms and look worse. The fix is length normalisation; the aggregation is a
   *modelling choice to validate on held-out data*, so it stays **pluggable** (no
   hardcoded pooling). Use `min` to catch the single weakest token (a transposed
   digit in an amount); use the geometric mean for overall field plausibility (the
   family Mistral OCR reports as `average_page_confidence_score`).
2. **It is uncalibrated** – and for RLHF’d LLMs *systematically overconfident*.
   Every signal here is a raw score; a [`Calibrator`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Calibrator) must run before
   any gate reads it.

Aggregators are registered under the `aggregators` namespace so a caller (or a
third party) can swap pooling by name.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import math
>>> logps = [math.log(0.9), math.log(0.8), math.log(0.95)]
>>> round(geo_mean(logps), 4)            # exp(mean log p)
0.8811
>>> round(min_prob(logps), 4)            # weakest token
0.8
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_LENGTH_ALPHA`](_autosummary/ek.qe.signals.html.md#ek.qe.signals.DEFAULT_LENGTH_ALPHA)   | Length-penalty exponent for [`length_normalized()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.signals.html.md#ek.qe.signals.length_normalized) (Wu et al. 2016 found `alpha` in `[0.6, 0.7]` best); a keyword default, never a magic constant.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DEFAULT_PROB_FLOOR`](_autosummary/ek.qe.signals.html.md#ek.qe.signals.DEFAULT_PROB_FLOOR)     | Smallest probability treated as non-zero.                                                                                                                                                          |

### Functions

| [`geo_mean`](_autosummary/ek.qe.signals.html.md#ek.qe.signals.geo_mean)(logps)                       | Geometric mean of token probabilities, `exp(mean log p)` (perplexity-inverse).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`length_normalized`](_autosummary/ek.qe.signals.html.md#ek.qe.signals.length_normalized)(logps, \*[, alpha]) | Length-normalised score `exp(Σ log p / T**alpha)` (tunable length penalty).      |

### ek.qe.signals.DEFAULT_LENGTH_ALPHA *= 0.6*

Length-penalty exponent for [`length_normalized()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.signals.html.md#ek.qe.signals.length_normalized) (Wu et al. 2016 found
`alpha` in `[0.6, 0.7]` best); a keyword default, never a magic constant.

### ek.qe.signals.DEFAULT_PROB_FLOOR *= 1e-12*

Smallest probability treated as non-zero. `log(p=0) = -inf` clamps to
`log(DEFAULT_PROB_FLOOR)` (mirrors the confidence floor) so a p=0 token still
drives min_prob/geo_mean toward 0 instead of being silently discarded.

# _autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md

# ek.qe.verifiers

Deterministic verifier signals – the cheapest, first-to-run QE layer.

Reference-free quality estimation should try the \*\*free, label-free, deterministic
checks first\*\* (`misc/docs/ek_03` §1d, §5; `ek_04` Layers 0-3): they cost
nothing, need no training data, and catch exactly the errors a confidence signal
misses – a value the extractor was *confident* about but that is structurally
impossible (a checksum that does not validate, a total that does not reconcile, an
enum value out of range). Only escalate to intrinsic confidence, agreement (ROVER),
or LLM signals on the residual that verifiers cannot settle.

The check primitives here (Luhn / IBAN / ISBN checksums, type/range/enum/regex,
cross-field reconciliation) are pure-Python and dependency-free *by design*: they
are reused both as reference-free [`Signal`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Signal) evidence (this module,
the [`ek.estimate_quality()`](_autosummary/ek.html.md#ek.estimate_quality) side) and – later – as the L1-L2 layers of the
flag-vs-correct validation pipeline (`ek/validate.py`, issue #7). Implementing the
checksums directly (rather than depending on the LGPL `python-stdnum`) keeps the
permissive-core promise intact.

A verifier emits raw evidence – a pass/fail [`Finding`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Finding) and a
fraction-passed score – never a calibrated probability or a decision.

### Example

```pycon
>>> luhn_check("79927398713")          # a classic Luhn-valid number
True
>>> luhn_check("79927398710")
False
>>> isbn_check("0-306-40615-2")         # ISBN-10
True
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_TOTALS_TOL`](_autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md#ek.qe.verifiers.DEFAULT_TOTALS_TOL)   | Default absolute tolerance for the cross-field totals reconciliation check.     |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CHECKSUMS`](_autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md#ek.qe.verifiers.CHECKSUMS)            | Built-in checksum checks, by name (register more under the `checks` namespace). |

### Functions

| [`checksum_validator`](_autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md#ek.qe.verifiers.checksum_validator)([kind, field_name, layer])     | A [`Validator`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Validator) that flags a value failing a named checksum.            |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`enum_validator`](_autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md#ek.qe.verifiers.enum_validator)(members, \*[, field_name, layer])  | A [`Validator`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Validator) that flags a value not in an allowed set.               |
| [`iban_check`](_autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md#ek.qe.verifiers.iban_check)(iban)                                  | IBAN validity via the ISO 13616 / ISO 7064 mod-97 rule (must equal 1).                                                                 |
| [`isbn10_check`](_autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md#ek.qe.verifiers.isbn10_check)(value)                               | ISBN-10 checksum (weighted mod-11; a trailing `X` counts as 10).                                                                       |
| [`isbn13_check`](_autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md#ek.qe.verifiers.isbn13_check)(value)                               | ISBN-13 / EAN-13 checksum (alternating 1/3 weights, mod-10).                                                                           |

|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ek.qe.verifiers.CHECKSUMS *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]]* *= {'iban': <function iban_check>, 'isbn': <function isbn_check>, 'isbn10': <function isbn10_check>, 'isbn13': <function isbn13_check>, 'luhn': <function luhn_check>}*

Built-in checksum checks, by name (register more under the `checks` namespace).

### ek.qe.verifiers.DEFAULT_TOTALS_TOL *= 0.01*

Default absolute tolerance for the cross-field totals reconciliation check.

### *class* ek.qe.verifiers.VerifierSignal(validators=list(), cost_tier=1)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Deterministic verifier evidence as a reference-free [`Signal`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Signal).

Cost tier 1 – the free, first-to-run layer. Runs a list of
[`Validator`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Validator) s on a value and returns the **fraction that passed**
in `[0, 1]` as the raw signal (`1.0` = every check passed). It also exposes
the [`Finding`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Finding) s it produced via [`findings()`](_autosummary/ek.qe.verifiers.html.md#ek.qe.verifiers.VerifierSignal.findings), so the same
object feeds both the score path (-> calibrate) and the audit path (-> review).
Like every signal it is uncalibrated: a verifier failing is strong evidence, not
a probability, so a [`Calibrator`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Calibrator) still runs before any gate.

### Example

```pycon
>>> v = VerifierSignal([checksum_validator("luhn")])
>>> v("79927398713")          # valid -> all checks pass
1.0
>>> v("79927398710")          # invalid -> the one check fails
0.0
```

#### findings(value, , spec=None)

All findings the validators produce for `value` (empty == all clear).

# _autosummary/ek.registry.html.md

# ek.registry

Strategy registry, optional-dependency guarding, and requirement checks.

`ek` is open-closed: every swappable behaviour (a [`Metric`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Metric), a
[`Signal`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Signal), a calibrator, an OCR backend, …) is registered under a
*namespace* and resolved by name. Built-in strategies register themselves at
import time; third parties add their own either by calling [`register()`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.register) or by
declaring an entry point in the `ek.<namespace>` group – no edit to `ek` needed.

Two more concerns live here so they stay out of the core logic:

- [`requires_extra()`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.requires_extra) – a decorator that turns a missing optional dependency
  into an *actionable* error (`pip install ek[ocr]`) instead of an opaque
  `ImportError` raised deep inside a call.
- [`check_requirements()`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.check_requirements) – a helper that reports, without raising, what an
  engine/feature needs (Python packages, system binaries, credentials), and
  defers to `ocracy`’s own doctor for OCR engines when it is installed.

### Example

```pycon
>>> @register("metrics", "shout")
... def shout(pred, gold, *, grammar=None):
...     return pred == gold
>>> get("metrics", "shout")("a", "a")
True
>>> "shout" in names("metrics")
True
```

### Functions

| [`check_requirements`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.check_requirements)(\*[, engine, extra])   | Report what an OCR engine or feature extra needs, without raising.      |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`get`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.get)(namespace, name)                      | Resolve a registered strategy by name (discovering entry points first). |
| [`names`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.names)(namespace)                          | All registered names in a namespace (after entry-point discovery).      |
| [`register`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.register)(namespace, name[, obj])          | Register `obj` under `namespace`/`name` (usable as a decorator).        |
| [`requires_extra`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.requires_extra)(extra, \*[, packages])     | Decorator: fail with an actionable install hint if an extra is missing. |
| [`resolve`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.resolve)(namespace, ref, \*[, default])    | Coerce a strategy reference to a callable.                              |

### Exceptions

| [`MissingExtraError`](_autosummary/ek.registry.html.md#ek.registry.MissingExtraError)   | Raised when an optional feature is used without its extra installed.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *exception* ek.registry.MissingExtraError

Bases: [`ImportError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ImportError)

Raised when an optional feature is used without its extra installed.

### ek.registry.check_requirements(, engine=None, extra=None)

Report what an OCR engine or feature extra needs, without raising.

For an OCR `engine` and an installed `ocracy`, defers to `ocracy`’s own
doctor (which knows each backend’s pip package, system binaries and
credentials). Otherwise returns a generic hint.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)
* **Returns:**
  A dict with at least `{"ok": bool, "hint": str}`.

### ek.registry.get(namespace, name)

Resolve a registered strategy by name (discovering entry points first).

* **Raises:**
  [**KeyError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#KeyError) – with the list of available names, if `name` is unknown.
* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

### ek.registry.names(namespace)

All registered names in a namespace (after entry-point discovery).

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### ek.registry.register(namespace, name, obj=None)

Register `obj` under `namespace`/`name` (usable as a decorator).

* **Parameters:**
  * **namespace** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A strategy family, e.g. `"metrics"`, `"signals"`,
    `"calibrators"`, `"policies"`, `"normalizers"`, `"ocr"`.
  * **name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The lookup key within the namespace.
  * **obj** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]) – The object to register; omit to use as a decorator.
* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)
* **Returns:**
  `obj` (so it can be used as a decorator).

### ek.registry.requires_extra(extra, , packages=None)

Decorator: fail with an actionable install hint if an extra is missing.

The wrapped callable runs only once every package in `packages` imports; the
common case (everything installed) adds a single cheap import check.

* **Parameters:**
  * **extra** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The extra name, used in the hint `pip install ek[<extra>]`.
  * **packages** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – Import names to probe (defaults to `[extra]`).
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)

### Example

```pycon
>>> @requires_extra("ocr", packages=["definitely_not_installed_pkg"])
... def run():
...     return "ran"
>>> try:
...     run()
... except MissingExtraError as e:
...     print("ek[ocr]" in str(e))
True
```

### ek.registry.resolve(namespace, ref, , default=None)

Coerce a strategy reference to a callable.

`ref` may be a registered name (`str`), an already-resolved object, or
`None` (in which case `default`, itself a name or object, is used).

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)


# _autosummary/ek.stores.html.md

# ek.stores

Local-file persistence for `ek`, as plain `MutableMapping` stores.

Everything `ek` persists – gold corpora, evaluation results, fitted
calibrators, human corrections, run logs – lives under the per-user data
directory `~/.local/share/ek/` (resolved cross-platform by
`config2py.AppData`), one subfolder per *kind*. Each store is a JSON
key-value store from `dol`: `store[key] = value` writes
`<kind>/<key>.json`, `store[key]` reads it back, iteration lists keys – so
callers get a dict-like facade rather than a bespoke god-class.

Progressive disclosure:

```pycon
>>> import tempfile; root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> s = json_store("gold", rootdir=root)
>>> s["doc-001"] = {"reference_text": "hello world"}
>>> s["doc-001"]["reference_text"]
'hello world'
>>> list(s)
['doc-001']
```

A [`mall()`](_autosummary/ek.stores.html.md#ek.stores.mall) groups every kind into one stores-of-stores mapping, with optional
`mall["gold", "doc-001"]` tuple-key access.

Tests and ephemeral use can redirect the root via the `rootdir` argument or the
`EK_DATA_HOME` environment variable, so nothing touches the real user folder.

### Module Attributes

| [`cache_this`](_autosummary/ek.stores.html.md#ek.stores.cache_this)([func, cache, key, pre_cache, ...])   | Unified caching decorator for properties and methods with persistent storage support.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`KINDS`](_autosummary/ek.stores.html.md#ek.stores.KINDS)                                            | The kinds of artifact `ek` persists; each becomes a subfolder + a store.                |

### Functions

| [`app_folder`](_autosummary/ek.stores.html.md#ek.stores.app_folder)()                                 | The root `ek` data folder (e.g. `~/.local/share/ek`).                                                       |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

| [`persistent_cache`](_autosummary/ek.stores.html.md#ek.stores.persistent_cache)([func, kind, key, rootdir]) | Memoize a plain function's result in a `kind` JSON store, across sessions.                                  |

### Classes

| [`Mall`](_autosummary/ek.stores.html.md#ek.stores.Mall)(\*[, kinds, rootdir])   | A read-only mapping of `kind -> json_store(kind)` (a dol "mall").   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ek.stores.KINDS *= ('gold', 'results', 'calibrators', 'corrections', 'runs', 'baselines')*

The kinds of artifact `ek` persists; each becomes a subfolder + a store.

### *class* ek.stores.Mall(, kinds=('gold', 'results', 'calibrators', 'corrections', 'runs', 'baselines'), rootdir=None)

Bases: [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)

A read-only mapping of `kind -> json_store(kind)` (a dol “mall”).

Supports both `mall["gold"]` (the store) and `mall["gold", key]` (the
value), the latter being sugar for `mall["gold"][key]`.

### ek.stores.app_folder()

The root `ek` data folder (e.g. `~/.local/share/ek`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### ek.stores.cache_this(func=None, , cache=None, key=None, pre_cache=False, as_property=None, ignore=None, serialize=None, deserialize=None)

Re-export for the idiomatic class-property persisted cache, e.g.
`@cache_this(cache=lambda self: json_store("runs"), key=...)` on a method.

### ek.stores.data_dir(kind, , rootdir=None)

Filesystem directory backing `kind` (under the data root or `rootdir`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### ek.stores.json_store(kind, , rootdir=None)

A JSON `MutableMapping` for one `kind` of artifact.

Keys are plain names (no extension); values are JSON-serializable objects.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### ek.stores.mall(, rootdir=None)

The full stores-of-stores mall (one JSON store per [`KINDS`](_autosummary/ek.stores.html.md#ek.stores.KINDS)).

* **Return type:**
  [`Mall`](_autosummary/ek.stores.html.md#ek.stores.Mall)

### ek.stores.persistent_cache(func=None, , kind='runs', key=None, rootdir=None)

Memoize a plain function’s result in a `kind` JSON store, across sessions.

Use as `@persistent_cache(kind="runs", key=...)`. Returned values must be
JSON-serializable. `key` may be a constant or a callable receiving the call
arguments; it defaults to the function’s qualified name (so provide a `key`
for functions that take arguments). For caching a *class property/method*,
prefer [`cache_this`](_autosummary/ek.stores.html.md#ek.stores.cache_this) (dol’s descriptor) instead.

### Example

```pycon
>>> import tempfile; root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> calls = []
>>> @persistent_cache(kind="runs", key="answer", rootdir=root)
... def compute():
...     calls.append(1)
...     return {"answer": 42}
>>> compute(), compute(), len(calls)
({'answer': 42}, {'answer': 42}, 1)
```


# _autosummary/ek.tools.html.md

# ek.tools

Small, CLI-friendly functions over the `ek` core (the dispatch surface).

These are thin, string-in/value-out wrappers designed for triple dispatch (CLI
today, HTTP/UI later). The single `_dispatch_funcs` list is the SSOT of what
`ek.__main__` exposes, so there is no duplicated command registration, and
each function’s *signature* is its command-line interface.

Run them from the shell:

```default
python -m ek cer "hello wrld" "hello world"
python -m ek where
python -m ek check tesseract
```

### Functions

| [`cer`](_autosummary/ek.tools.html.md#ek.tools.cer)(prediction, gold, \*[, normalize])         | Character Error Rate between a prediction and a gold string (lower is better).     |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check`](_autosummary/ek.tools.html.md#ek.tools.check)(engine)                                  | Report what an OCR engine needs to run (delegates to ocracy when installed).       |
| [`cost_per_success`](_autosummary/ek.tools.html.md#ek.tools.cost_per_success)(total_dollars, successes, \*) | Cost-of-Pass: dollars per *successfully completed* task (`inf` if none succeeded). |
| [`engines`](_autosummary/ek.tools.html.md#ek.tools.engines)()                                      | List installed OCR backends (requires the `ek[ocr]` extra).                        |
| [`pass_k`](_autosummary/ek.tools.html.md#ek.tools.pass_k)(n, c[, k])                              | pass@k (capability) and pass^k (reliability) from `c` successes in `n` trials.     |
| [`rover`](_autosummary/ek.tools.html.md#ek.tools.rover)(\*hypotheses[, confidence])              | ROVER-fuse 2+ transcriptions into a consensus + mean agreement (reference-free).   |
| [`version`](_autosummary/ek.tools.html.md#ek.tools.version)()                                      | Print the installed `ek` version.                                                  |
| [`wer`](_autosummary/ek.tools.html.md#ek.tools.wer)(prediction, gold, \*[, normalize])         | Word Error Rate between a prediction and a gold string (lower is better).          |
| [`where`](_autosummary/ek.tools.html.md#ek.tools.where)()                                        | Print the local data folder where `ek` persists gold/results/runs.                 |

### ek.tools.cer(prediction, gold, , normalize=None)

Character Error Rate between a prediction and a gold string (lower is better).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### ek.tools.check(engine)

Report what an OCR engine needs to run (delegates to ocracy when installed).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ek.tools.cost_per_success(total_dollars, successes, , attempts=None)

Cost-of-Pass: dollars per *successfully completed* task (`inf` if none succeeded).

The unit that matters for an agent – tokens spent on a failed episode are pure waste.

Example:

```default
python -m ek cost-per-success 12.50 5 --attempts 20
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ek.tools.engines()

List installed OCR backends (requires the `ek[ocr]` extra).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

### ek.tools.pass_k(n, c, k=1)

pass@k (capability) and pass^k (reliability) from `c` successes in `n` trials.

`pass@k` asks “can it *ever* do this?”; `pass^k` asks “does it do this *every* time?”
– and only the second is a production number.

Example:

```default
python -m ek pass-k 10 9 --k 8      # a 90%-reliable agent, judged over 8 trials
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ek.tools.rover(\*hypotheses, confidence=True)

ROVER-fuse 2+ transcriptions into a consensus + mean agreement (reference-free).

Example:

```default
python -m ek rover "the cat sat" "the cat sit" "the bat sat"
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ek.tools.version()

Print the installed `ek` version.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ek.tools.wer(prediction, gold, , normalize=None)

Word Error Rate between a prediction and a gold string (lower is better).

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### ek.tools.where()

Print the local data folder where `ek` persists gold/results/runs.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/ek.validate.html.md

# ek.validate

Reference-free post-extraction validation & correction (issue #7).

A layered, **cheapest -> most-expensive** pipeline with an explicit
**FLAG-vs-CORRECT** distinction (`misc/docs/ek_04`). Every method estimates
`argmax_v P(v|o)` without a gold reference: the prior `P(v)` strengthens in
layers – schema/type/range (cheapest, strongest), then lexicon/gazetteer, then
language-model surprisal (softest) – with cross-field consistency and statistical
anomaly checks on top.

The single most important architectural line is **FLAG vs CORRECT**:

- A **Validator** only *flags*: it yields [`Finding`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Finding) s with
  `severity=FLAG` and never rewrites the value. The deterministic verifier layer
  (`ek.qe.verifiers`: checksums, regex, range, enum, schema, totals) is re-exported
  here so a caller composes the whole stack from one place.
- A **Corrector** can also *correct*: it yields a `severity=CORRECT` Finding whose
  `suggestion` is the proposed replacement. Only a narrow, safe, deterministic
  class corrects automatically – canonicalization (L0) and closed-set lexicon
  resolution (L2); free invention is reserved for the gated L5 neural corrector.

Both share one callable shape – `(value, *, spec) -> Iterable[Finding]` – so
[`validation_pipeline()`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.validation_pipeline) composes them uniformly. A CORRECT finding’s suggestion
is applied to the value *before the next layer runs* (the noisy-channel chain: a
cheap deterministic fix short-circuits the expensive layers), and an injectable
`stop_when` policy ends the pass early (e.g. once a value is corrected or clean).

The deterministic layers here need no extra dependencies (`rapidfuzz` is core). The
softer/heavier layers ship as **dependency-injected** layers: the layer is dep-free
and you inject the model/LLM call (your in-domain LM scorer, your LLM client), so the
expensive backend is your deployment choice, not a default dependency.

- **L3 LM surprisal** (FLAG): [`lm_surprisal_validator()`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.lm_surprisal_validator) takes an injected
  `(str) -> float` surprisal scorer (n-gram / masked-LM PLL, e.g. `minicons`) and
  flags low-probability spans. Statistical anomaly without an LM:
  [`benford_findings()`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.benford_findings) (leading-digit) and [`zscore_anomaly_findings()`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.zscore_anomaly_findings)
  > (robust median/MAD magnitude outliers), both dep-free.
- **L5 neural/LLM correction** (CORRECT, gated): [`llm_corrector()`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.llm_corrector) takes an
  injected `(str) -> Optional[str]` correction call; it is the only layer that
  invents content, so it fires only on already-flagged values (`only_flagged`),
  reads the pipeline’s findings, and keeps the original for audit.
- **L4 constrained generation** is a *generation*-time concern (it constrains a
  generative extractor, not post-hoc output – ek_04 separates “constrain-on-generate”
  from “post-hoc validation”), so it lives on the extraction side
  (`ek[constrained]`: `outlines`/XGrammar/`instructor`), not in this pipeline.

### Example

```pycon
>>> from ek.validate import validation_pipeline, lexicon_corrector, stop_on_correction
>>> from ek.base import Severity
>>> fix = validation_pipeline(
...     lexicon_corrector(["France", "Germany", "Spain"]),
...     stop_when=stop_on_correction,
... )
>>> r = fix("Frnace")               # one transposition from a closed enum
>>> r.value
'France'
>>> r.corrected
True
>>> r.findings[0].severity is Severity.CORRECT
True
```

Default minimum similarity (`rapidfuzz` ratio in [0, 1]) for a closed-set lexicon
match to be auto-applied as a correction rather than flagged. 0.8 catches typical
single-edit and transposition typos (“Frnace”->”France” ~0.83) while the wide gap
to an unrelated word (~0.3) keeps false corrections rare.

### ek.validate.benford_findings(numbers, , field='', tol=0.15, min_n=30, layer='anomaly')

FLAG a numeric field whose first-digit distribution deviates from Benford’s law.

A reference-free anomaly check for naturally-occurring magnitudes (amounts,
populations, counts): the first significant digit should follow
`P(d)=log10(1+1/d)`. A large deviation flags fabricated or systematically-wrong
data. **Corpus-level** (takes the whole column of values) and **FLAG-only** – it
routes a field to review, never auto-edits, and can false-positive on legitimately
bounded/skewed fields. Skipped (returns `[]`) below `min_n` usable values,
since the law is asymptotic.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

### ek.validate.canonicalize_corrector(normalize, , field_name='', layer='canonicalize')

L0: fold a value to canonical form, emitting a CORRECT finding when it changes.

`normalize` is anything [`ek.canonicalize.resolve_canonicalizer()`](_autosummary/ek.canonicalize.html.md#ek.canonicalize.resolve_canonicalizer) accepts
(a registered name, a callable, a step list). The narrowest, safest corrector –
run it first so later layers compare canonical forms.

* **Return type:**
  [`Corrector`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.Corrector)

### ek.validate.cross_field_validator(predicate, , message, fields=(), layer='cross_field')

FLAG a record when `predicate(record)` is False (a general cross-field check).

Skips silently when `predicate` raises on a partial record (a missing field is
not itself a cross-field violation).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Finding)]]

### ek.validate.lexicon_corrector(vocabulary, , threshold=0.8, scorer=None, field_name='', layer='lexicon', flag_unmatched=True)

L2: resolve a value against a **closed** vocabulary by fuzzy match (`rapidfuzz`).

The safest corrector in the stack when the candidate set is closed (country codes,
SKUs, enums): an exact member passes untouched; a single close match
(similarity `>= threshold`) is applied as a CORRECT finding; otherwise the value
is FLAGged as out-of-vocabulary (when `flag_unmatched`). Against an *open*
vocabulary, set `flag_unmatched=False` and treat matches as suggestions only.

* **Parameters:**
  * **vocabulary** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The closed set of valid values.
  * **threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Minimum `rapidfuzz` similarity in `[0, 1]` to auto-correct.
  * **scorer** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – A `rapidfuzz` scorer (default `fuzz.ratio`).
  * **flag_unmatched** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – FLAG a value with no close match (default `True`).
* **Return type:**
  [`Corrector`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.Corrector)

### ek.validate.llm_corrector(correct_fn, , only_flagged=True, field_name='', layer='llm_correct')

L5: a **gated** neural/LLM corrector – the only layer that invents content.

`correct_fn` is an **injected** `(value) -> Optional[str]` (bring your own
LLM/seq2seq call; return a corrected string, or `None` to leave the value
unchanged). It is the most expensive and stochastic layer, so by default
(`only_flagged`) it fires \*\*only on a value that a cheaper layer already
FLAGged\*\* – gate it to the residual, never let it silently rewrite clean fields
(this layer reads the pipeline’s accumulated findings via `wants_findings`).
Emits a CORRECT finding; the pipeline applies the rewrite and keeps the original
for audit. Always verify its output downstream – it can make text worse.

Recipe (Anthropic): `correct_fn=lambda v: client.messages.create(model=...,
messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt(v)}]).content[0].text.strip()` with
`client = anthropic.Anthropic()` (MIT). Constrain/verify the result and keep an
audit trail.

* **Return type:**
  [`Corrector`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.Corrector)

### ek.validate.lm_surprisal_validator(scorer, , threshold, higher_is_worse=True, field_name='', layer='lm_prior')

L3: FLAG a value whose language-model surprisal crosses `threshold`.

`scorer` is an **injected** `(str) -> float` returning a surprisal /
perplexity / negative-log-likelihood (dependency injection: bring your own
in-domain n-gram or masked-LM scorer – an *in-domain* prior is what makes this
useful). FLAG-only on its own; pair it with a candidate generator
(`lexicon_corrector` / `llm_corrector`) to actually correct. Set
`higher_is_worse=False` if your scorer returns a probability (higher = better).

Recipe (masked-LM pseudo-log-likelihood): wrap `minicons` –
`from minicons import scorer; m = scorer.MaskedLMScorer("bert-base-uncased", "cpu")`
– and pass `scorer=lambda s: -m.sequence_score([s])[0]` (surprisal = negative
PLL). `minicons` is MIT; install your own LM backend (it pulls torch).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Finding)]]

### ek.validate.ordering_validator(keys, , strict=True, layer='cross_field')

FLAG a record whose comparable values at `keys` are not ascending.

The canonical date/sequence check (`start <= end`, issue before due). Only the
keys actually present and mutually comparable are checked, so it is safe on
partial records.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/ek.base.html.md#ek.base.Finding)]]

### ek.validate.stop_on_correction(findings)

Stop policy: end the pass as soon as any layer proposes a correction.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### ek.validate.stop_on_flag(findings)

Stop policy: end the pass at the first FLAG (fail fast).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### ek.validate.validate(value, \*, layers=(), spec=None, apply_corrections=True, stop_when=<function \_never_stop>)

Run one value through a validation/correction pipeline (progressive disclosure).

The simple call `validate(v, layers=[...])` Just Works; tune the correction
behaviour with `apply_corrections`/`stop_when`. Compose `layers` from the
factories in this module (`canonicalize_corrector`, `lexicon_corrector`, the
re-exported verifier validators) in cheapest-first order.

* **Return type:**
  [`ValidationResult`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.ValidationResult)

### ek.validate.validation_pipeline(\*layers, apply_corrections=True, stop_when=<function \_never_stop>)

Compose validators/correctors into a cheapest -> most-expensive pipeline.

`layers` run in the given order (the order encodes the cost spine). Each layer
is a `(value, *, spec) -> Iterable[Finding]` callable. When `apply_corrections`
(default), the first `CORRECT` finding a layer emits is applied to the value
before the next layer runs – so a cheap deterministic fix is what the expensive
layers then see (the noisy-channel chain). `stop_when` is an injectable
early-exit policy over the findings accumulated so far (see
[`stop_on_correction()`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.stop_on_correction) / [`stop_on_flag()`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.stop_on_flag)); the default runs every layer.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`ValidationResult`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.ValidationResult)]

### ek.validate.zscore_anomaly_findings(numbers, , field='', threshold=3.5, min_n=30, layer='anomaly')

FLAG numeric values that are robust-z-score outliers (median + MAD based).

A reference-free, **dependency-free** anomaly check that complements
[`benford_findings()`](_autosummary/ek.validate.html.md#ek.validate.benford_findings) (which checks the leading-digit *distribution*; this
checks individual *magnitudes*). For a numeric column it computes each value’s
**modified z-score** – `0.6745 * (x - median) / MAD` – which is robust to the
very outliers it is looking for, and FLAGs those whose absolute score exceeds
`threshold`. One FLAG per outlying value (carrying its index); **FLAG-only** –
it routes a value to review, never edits. Skipped below `min_n` (robust
statistics on a handful of points are noise). When the MAD is 0 (a *near*-constant
column, e.g. many identical values plus one outlier) it falls back to the
mean-absolute-deviation scale (Iglewicz & Hoaglin), so a lone outlier is still
caught; a *truly* constant column (no spread at all) yields no findings. For
*multivariate* outliers, plug an isolation forest via `pyod` (already in
`ek[validation]`) as a custom validator.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

# ai-agents.html.md

# For AI agents

`ek` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `ek-dev-add-metric`

How to add a reference-based (offline) metric to ek’s score() side — the output-type to metric to library decision table (CER/WER via jiwer, ANLS\*/anls_star, span-F1 via seqeval/nervaluate, TEDS/GriTS for tables, cost-weighted typed-graph GED via networkx/apted/zss, coref via metametric), the Metric Protocol **call**(pred, gold, \*, grammar=None) -> float, the Report/Score decomposition object, how to wrap a library behind the Protocol and register it, and the flagship cost-weighted typed-graph must-build whose weights come from Layer-A importance. Use when implementing, wrapping, registering, choosing, or debugging an offline/reference-based metric, scoring pred vs gold, slot/entity F1, table TEDS, graph edit distance, ANLS, WER/CER, canonicalization-before-scoring, match schemes, or per-slice/per-path TP/FP/FN. For online/reference-free confidence, calibration, and decisions use the estimate_quality side instead.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/ek ek-dev-add-metric --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ek-dev-add-metric`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ek/tree/HEAD/skills/ek-dev-add-metric).

### `ek-dev-add-signal`

How to add a reference-free quality-estimation component to ek’s online estimate_quality() side: a new Signal (deterministic verifier / intrinsic-confidence / logprob / agreement-ROVER / auxiliary-QE / LLM-judge), a Calibrator (Platt/Temperature/Isotonic), or a DecisionPolicy/SelectivePolicy (ConformalGate / RiskControlGate / CostSensitiveGate). Use when building or extending the signal->calibrate->decide pipeline, wiring a Strategy Protocol into the registry, adding confidence/uncertainty/agreement signals, ROVER voting, conformal prediction (MAPIE/crepes/TorchCP), calibration (netcal/sklearn), ECE/D-ECE, risk-coverage curves, or selective prediction / accept-flag-block gating for extraction or OCR quality. Not for offline reference-based metrics (that is the score()/add-metric side).

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/ek ek-dev-add-signal --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ek-dev-add-signal`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ek/tree/HEAD/skills/ek-dev-add-signal).

### `ek-dev-agents`

How to build and extend ek’s AGENT/ASSISTANT evaluation instance (ek/agents/) — the second concrete instance after ek.ocr. Covers the episode object (Episode/Trajectory/Step/Cost/RunProvenance as Layer B) and the task/tool grammar (ToolSpec/TaskSpec building a GraphGrammar as Layer A, where FieldSpec.importance is the cost of a wrong tool argument), the agent metrics (TaskSuccessMetric with an injected Checker oracle, CostPerSuccessMetric implementing Cost-of-Pass E[cost]/P(success), ToolCallMetric doing BFCL AST match over a multiset of calls, TrajectoryMetric doing a Needleman-Wunsch sequence edit distance), the reliability estimators (pass@k capability vs pass^k reliability — pure functions, NOT Metrics), the LLM-as-judge seams (JudgeSignal reference-free vs JudgeMetric reference-based vs pairwise_judge, plus judge_validation reusing Krippendorff/Cohen IAA), the agent harness (run_suite with k trials, and the variance-aware agent_regression_gate using Wilson/bootstrap intervals), and the duck-typed bridges (trajectory_from_messages, from_inspect_sample). Use when implementing, debugging, or extending anything under ek/agents/, adding an agent metric/signal/checker, scoring an episode or trajectory or tool call, computing pass^k or cost per successful task, evaluating an LLM judge, or wiring an external agent harness (Inspect AI, DeepEval, Ragas). Read BEFORE touching ek/agents/.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/ek ek-dev-agents --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ek-dev-agents`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ek/tree/HEAD/skills/ek-dev-agents).

### `ek-dev-architecture`

Master orientation map for developers BUILDING ek (a framework for building Knowledge Evaluation systems that evaluate information-extraction outputs; OCR is the noisiest special case). Read this FIRST before touching any ek component. Covers the two-need 2x2 (reference-based vs reference-free, instance vs system), the two-layer data model (Layer A GraphGrammar schema/cost SSOT + Layer B AnnotatedExtraction metadata), the facades score()/evaluate()/estimate_quality(), the strategy-Protocol + registry + dependency-injection + requires_extra open-closed pattern, the module layout (base, registry, stores, metrics, canonicalize, qe/rover, validate, harness, ocr, tools, **main**), the config2py.AppData + dol persistence model, the must-builds (two-layer object, cost-weighted typed-graph distance, ROVER), and a which-report-for-which-component table. Use when deciding where code goes, what a component is named, how facades share the Layer-A object, how strategies plug in, or which ek_0N report to read.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/ek ek-dev-architecture --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ek-dev-architecture`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ek/tree/HEAD/skills/ek-dev-architecture).

### `ek-dev-licensing`

Licensing guardrail for ek developers: consult BEFORE adding ANY dependency. Covers the license-tiering policy (lean permissive core vs opt-in extras), the register of 6 license landmines (GPL Levenshtein/python-Levenshtein, LGPL TorchCP, non-commercial surya-ocr, GPL Potato, proprietary Prodigy) with their permissive replacements, scanner-invisible traps where license terms live in repo files not PyPI metadata (zss BSD-3, mistralai namespace pkg, PubTabNet CDLA), the rule that nothing copyleft or non-commercial is ever a default, and the CI license gate (pip-licenses/reuse) that fails the build on GPL/AGPL/non-commercial in core..hitl. Use when picking a metric/calibration/validation/OCR/agreement/HITL backend, adding to pyproject extras, choosing an edit-distance or conformal or annotation library, hitting a “GPL”/”non-commercial”/”RAIL”/”copyleft” license, deciding which extra a dep belongs in, or whether a dep needs import-only quarantine.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/ek ek-dev-licensing --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ek-dev-licensing`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ek/tree/HEAD/skills/ek-dev-licensing).

### `ek-dev-ocr`

Build and maintain ek’s OCR evaluation layer on top of the ocracy package — the concrete instance of ek’s reference-based score() and reference-free estimate_quality() facades applied to image->OcrResult engines. Use when working on the ek[ocr] optional extra, wiring or running the OCR offline benchmark (CER/WER/ANLS per-slice over a gold corpus), mapping OcrResult/TextBlock into AnnotatedExtraction/FieldEstimate, deciding which ocracy backend to evaluate, handling null-safe VLM engines (Claude/GPT-4o/Mistral/Mathpix returning text-only, blocks=[], confidence=None), reading per-engine capability profiles (who emits real vs model-guessed geometry, who is calibrated, who emits TEDS-able tables), gating remote engines that make paid API calls, dealing with the missing normalized table type, or anything touching ek<->ocracy. Enforces the dependency-direction rule: ek depends on ocracy via an extra; never ocracy->ek; ek core depends only on the OcrResult shape so it evaluates any image->OcrResult callable.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/ek ek-dev-ocr --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/ek-dev-ocr`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ek/tree/HEAD/skills/ek-dev-ocr).
